answer: Each agent identity must be bound to a remote-attestation key from a distinct hardware enclave, signed by the chip vendor, and the registry admits one identity per device key. A garden of fake agents on one server shares one key and so gets one seat. To field 1,000 sybils an attacker must buy and run 1,000 separate attested chips, a cost that climbs like a ridge with every identity, and device keys found leaked or reused are revoked network-wide, so one rising tide of exposure wipes out the whole farm at once.
